# Architecture

<!-- awf:edit overview: from .awf/docs/parts/architecture/overview.md -->
## Overview
awf renders tracked workflow guidance from `.awf/`, while its binary owns immutable schema-2 effort residents, optional mutable protocol-2 activity, and stateless optional managed-worktree operations at the repository primary control root. A workflow carries one slug and owned memory only when durable continuity materially helps; Git remains the worktree topology authority. Core `effort-workflow` owns creation through finish and directs runtimes without supplied effort paths into the exact existing awf-managed worktree, while explicit-path runtimes may remain at the repository root and target it by path. Pi derives a capability-gated direct association extension: one process-local owner attaches activity without changing CWD, caches fixed memory/worktree facts for transient context, and publishes complete advisory Remote Pi metadata independently from a display-only effort suffix. Authoritative capability snapshots, synchronous replay, and lifecycle clears affect presentation only and never routing identity. Generated Pi handoff remains independent bounded-prose session replacement; it accepts no effort input and never selects an effort or mutates lifecycle state.
Schema-31 migration retires lock-resident ADR routing values; authored ADR format remains the parser authority.

Pi context usage is a standalone observation extension: it injects current model-window and active-branch compaction facts before each model call; handoff retains replacement mechanics while translating accepted kickoff once into a visible `agent-handoff` custom message at the replacement boundary, and subagents retain child execution.

## Components
- `internal/testsupport` owns isolated TestMain-home allocation, conservative stale cleanup, logical-byte accounting, and deterministic human result rendering while remaining a standard-library-only leaf. Its `cmd/testtmpclean` subpackage owns only the repo-private cleanup command's parsing, force warning, output routing, and exit mapping; keeping the command beneath the test-support boundary prevents ordinary production packages from importing test support.
- `internal/effort` owns schema-2 immutable `.awf/efforts/<slug>/state.json`, always-owned `memory.md`, optional protocol-2 advisory `activity.json`, durable publication, and restartable finish tombstones. Activity is an owner-checked Pi-session claim, never worktree topology, authorization, or a lock.
- `internal/worktree` owns stateless add, integrate, and restartable safe removal over `.awf/worktrees/<slug>/` and `awf/<slug>`. It reaches Git only through a narrow consumer-owned contract the composition root binds to the seam, so it holds worktree policy and no Git mechanism.
- `internal/git` is the one semantic Git seam: every capability the rest of awf needs is an entrypoint on its handle or one of its free functions, and whether an entrypoint uses go-git or the git binary is an internal detail with no consumer-visible trace. It owns the isolated, deadline-refusing runner, the seam error vocabulary, and the tolerant open path. Its committed-tree seam can enumerate sorted project-relative path and mode metadata without reading blobs, then fail closed while reading an exact selected path set. Two repo-walking tests fail on any Git library import or git subprocess constructed outside it.
- `internal/snapshot` owns both complete immutable `Tree` values and type-distinct immutable `Selection` values. They share one validating, cloning, sorting file-set core, but no conversion lets a sparse selection acquire complete-tree absence semantics. Current and staged consumers retain complete trees; historical audit consumes only an explicit selection.
- `internal/filesystem` owns the one production `os.Root`-backed handle; consumers own local structural contracts and policy helpers, while `internal/testsupport/fsfixture` is the distinct standard-library-only kernel-backed fault source.
- `internal/adr` owns ADR identity, intrinsic format parsing, Decision-item exact-source retention and stable identity, lifecycle validation, and the ordered activation registry that selects the current authoring marker. A future format adds its parser and transition matrix, registers its schema activation, updates scaffolding, and proves older formats remain readable without adding a number cutoff.
- `internal/currentstate` owns one pairing resolver for transition checks and provisional older-format introduction detection. Its reduced file-set core assembles ADR records and source bytes plus topic definitions and claims from either a complete tree or an explicit selection without constructing marker indexes or domain ownership, while working-tree and staged loaders retain the full projection. Staged checking reports an older introduction without suppressing any other derivable violation; definitive incoming-parent and message qualification belongs to the later `commit-msg` boundary.
- `internal/audit` owns one immutable historical operation per invocation: incremental commit and aggregate rule state, compact replay records, deterministic child-before-parent replay scheduling, live cleanliness, transition replay, stale-merge replay, and an alias-aware revision store. It validates compact graph identity, cycles, and direct boundary parents before loading authority, then interleaves each commit's stale and transition work in lexicographic-revision schedule order while separately buffering their externally ordered findings. It consumes the Git seam's one rich-commit visitor without acquiring Git policy; after observation it retains grouped ordinary findings and compact replay evidence only. A light revision load enumerates metadata, reads config and an optional lock, and derives the committed docs layout and exact authority paths. Its one-shot heavy loader reads and parses that selection only when a consumer needs a universe, then drops captured selection bytes. Revision keys separately alias canonical entries when conservative first-parent relevance permits; per-key consumer accounting aggregates aliases, clears source evidence after its last stale use, and clears parsed universes and cached heavy errors at their final use. `.awf` changes, changes under the parent's committed decisions directory, merge first-parent changes, and ambiguous evidence remain distinct, while a parent outside the range loads directly as a cached boundary.
- `internal/plan` owns legacy, plan-v1 compatibility, and plan-v2 source-set parsing, typed structural validation, exact filename-or-stem and numeric selector resolution, and executable-closure Markdown rendering without source mutation.
- `internal/config` owns the optional typed `commitPolicy` schema and its structural validation; `internal/configspec` owns its adopter-facing field descriptions. The block is absent-safe, and this repository activates exact owner identity plus SSH-signature checks after its published boundary.
- `internal/commitpolicy` owns exact commit facts, policy evaluation, typed outcomes, and their single human rendering. `internal/project` composes it with the Git seam for one explicit-target verifier; `cmd/awf` routes `awf check commit-policy` without reconstructing its presentation. The rendered reference-transaction and pre-push payloads call that verifier, while adopter-owned worktree-aware stubs and GitHub branch protection own the local and remote boundaries.
- `internal/projectlicense` owns verification of the root project's exact AGPL-3.0-only license bytes, public README references, and GoReleaser archive inclusion; `cmd/releasecheck` composes that policy before its changelog checks.
- `internal/migrate` applies schema upgrades, including the byte-preserving commit-policy generation, the read-only preflight and journaled reset that retire obsolete disposable residents.
- `internal/upgrade` owns the recoverable upgrade journal: tracked file images, proven resident-tree quarantine, and the lock replacement that commits every schema advance.
- Generated Pi extensions provide governed subagent dispatch and effort-state-independent bounded-prose session handoff. Handoff owns the one translation from accepted kickoff to its visible `agent-handoff` custom envelope and replacement-bound turn trigger; no custom renderer or provider-role claim is added. When selected `effort-workflow` meets an enabled Pi target, the target-owned `awf-effort` client alone invokes the binary activity and owner-scoped memory protocols, while its index owns direct process-local association, immutable snapshots, dynamic associated-memory tool activation, local serialization, Pi file-queue participation, heartbeat/shutdown cleanup, complete advisory metadata, and capability-gated display-suffix publication. The binary owns memory parsing, exact body matching, timestamps, and durable publication; command code chooses ordinary shared presentation or the required machine protocol; the generated client owns bounded transport and strict decoding. Capability snapshots authoritatively replace suffix support, replay and lifecycle boundaries publish the current slug or null synchronously, optional event failures degrade to metadata-only behavior, and no presentation value changes routing identity; no non-Pi target receives those artifacts.
- `internal/resident` owns resident-root policy below the sync core: the closed table of roots the primary control root owns, the resident path and render-kind predicates, the anchoring `Roots` value that resolves every output path, and the collision and uninstall lifecycle. A structural test fails on any resident root name spelled, or table shape redeclared, under `internal/project` or `cmd/`.
- `internal/execution` selects closed operation steps, prepares their requirement closure once, binds typed consumer actions, and executes deterministic outcomes. It imports only the standard library and owns no consumer capability value or presentation policy.
- `internal/project` composes parsed working and index plan corpora with ADR identity and Decision source blocks for blocking links, Proposed-only assignment notes, and read projection inputs; task-projected Phase close and Advances/Completes remain constraints, not transferred ownership.
- `internal/project.Loader` owns project-opening policy: configuration validation, target resolution, effective-catalog derivation, and catalog conformance over explicitly supplied dependencies. The wider `internal/project` package is the sync core: render pipeline, output plan, drift check, current-state and topics, sweep, validate, the kind and target tables, layout, config reference, scaffold, and sync orchestration. It resolves audit settings and layout as an outer composition point but owns no historical range or revision cache. A check creates one operation-scoped parsed-plan set, constructs one operation-owned output plan, and projects those shared values into blocking findings and advisories, while plan reads resolve the configured plans directory and delegate typed parsing and rendering to `internal/plan`. For context it keeps only the loading half, exposed as one assembled context-state value with two core-side constructors, one over an opened project and one over a staged tree.
- `internal/contextq` owns the context query above the sync core: request-sensitive assembly from that one state value, tier-0 directory orientation, actual marker-kind file and directory relationships, topic-level authority expansion, artifact-sensitive grouping, the context and uncovered result vocabulary, and the human rendering of both reports. A structural test fails if the core's exported surface carries context result vocabulary or if this package reaches past the state seam.
- `cmd/awf` is the composition root for top-level and post-mutation render, and composes typed repository-check capabilities through `internal/execution`: the `runSync` family selects the production config loader, standard catalog, and semantic resident-root resolver before constructing `internal/project.Loader`. It exposes protocol-2 effort activity JSON and owner-scoped memory protocol v1 as required machine bypasses; ordinary sync, effort, and worktree outcomes arrive as package-owned presentation documents while the command retains argument handling, stream selection, and exit mapping. It also routes bounded project checks; for context and parsed-plan reads it owns only argument handling, output routing, and exit mapping while the owning package renders the report or executable closure. `cmd/contextspilllog`, `cmd/covercheck`, `cmd/pincheck`, `cmd/releasecheck`, and `cmd/repoaudit` provide repo-owned supporting checks, while `internal/testsupport/cmd/testtmpclean` provides the test-support-owned cleanup command.
- `internal/manifest` accepts retired ADR routing keys only for schema-30-and-earlier compatibility decoding; `internal/migrate` generation 31 removes them without rewriting ADRs, while `internal/upgrade` discards the frozen bridge payload at its existing journal commit point.

- Generated Pi extensions have separate owners: context usage injects transient model-window and active-branch compaction facts, handoff replaces the parent session with agent-owned custom context, and subagents manage child execution and routing.

## Data flow
The invoking checkout supplies tracked configuration and native workflow skills. The optional typed `commitPolicy` mapping is parsed and structurally validated by `internal/config`, then projected into render data and only into the config hashes of templates that consume it; an absent mapping supplies no values or activation. Schema generation 34 is byte-preserving for trees without this optional mapping. For render and post-mutation render, `runSync` selects config-tree loading, the immutable standard catalog, and semantic resident-root resolution at the executable boundary, then injects them into `internal/project.Loader`; the Loader validates configuration, resolves targets, derives the effective catalog, and checks conformance. Native Git resolves one primary control root. Effort creation validates and exclusively reserves the caller-supplied short slug directory independently from the title, publishes `memory.md` before static `state.json`, syncs each boundary, and then by default orchestrates the standalone managed-worktree Add, rolling back through restartable finish only on proven-absent topology; enumeration ignores unpublished directories but preserves foreign bytes. Managed worktree commands derive path and branch from the slug and re-read actual Git path, registration, branch, cleanliness, operation, identity, and ancestry facts before each mutation. Pi handoff revalidates only its pending request and persisted session, then translates accepted kickoff once into a visible `agent-handoff` custom envelope and triggers the replacement turn; workflow guidance owns checkpoint reorientation. `internal/resident` holds the one table naming the resident roots the primary control root owns, `.awf/efforts` and `.awf/worktrees`, and output planning, render, drift, backup detection, current-state and context discovery, sweep, nested-adopter filtering, install, and uninstall all read it through that package; each root contributes exactly one governed self-ignoring `.gitignore`, and no consumer recurses into or deletes a dynamic descendant. Retiring a root is a schema migration: generation 22 classifies every legacy leaf read-only, refuses while any legacy managed worktree fact or unprovable resident remains, and otherwise quarantines the proven residents in one journaled transaction whose final lock replacement is the commit point. For context requests, the project snapshot classifies selected paths, preserves actual `State`, `Touches`, and `Proofs` relationships, expands authority only through the requested tier or facets, and delivers direct or secure spill output unchanged. A project check parses the configured plans directory once, constructs one output plan, and projects the same typed set into blocking structure findings and commit-scope advisories. Repository checks prepare working config as a foundation, conditionally prepare a Project and working reports or a stage-0 index, bind typed actions, then execute direct or aggregate selections in stable order. The working project/filesystem, working current-state, and stage-0 index remain distinct source universes. `awf read plan` resolves an exact filename or stem and canonical phase or task selector through `internal/project`, then writes `internal/plan`'s source-ordered executable closure unchanged.

At release time, `cmd/releasecheck` first delegates the root project-license contract to `internal/projectlicense`, which verifies the canonical AGPL-3.0-only bytes, README references, and GoReleaser archive configuration without treating dependency metadata or retained third-party notices as project-license inputs. Only then does the command enforce its changelog pin.

An explicit `awf check commit-policy <revision-or-range>...` invocation opens the invoking worktree's project, expands and deduplicates commits after its configured baseline through `internal/git`, evaluates exact identities and optional SSH signing through `internal/commitpolicy`, and writes the package-owned result. An absent policy is a successful disabled preview note; operational refusals retain their category and reconciliation actions. This repository configures the published boundary, exact owner identity, and pinned SSH signer. Its adopter-owned stubs resolve the invoking worktree and delegate branch transactions to the generated reference-transaction payload; pre-push expands commit-bearing branch and recursively peeled tag targets through the same verifier before the gate. GitHub then enforces signed commits at the final `main` boundary.

Every catalog skill, including `effort-workflow`, renders for both built-in targets. The target-neutral guide directs native persistent checkout or context tooling to the exact existing `.awf/worktrees/<slug>` checkout and never creates a parallel harness-owned worktree. Pi alone derives `using-effort` and the extension from the catalog relationship. Its explicit attach or detach request invokes the protocol-v2 binary directly from the repository root without changing CWD; the process-local association supplies fixed relative memory and optional managed-worktree paths in transient context, and restart begins detached. Remote Pi metadata is complete advisory replacement data and remains independent from optional display-suffix publication. Complete capability snapshots authoritatively enable or withdraw suffix support; attach or late support publishes the canonical slug, replay answers synchronously, and lifecycle boundaries publish null. Missing listeners, withdrawn support, or failed optional emissions degrade to metadata-only behavior without reading, composing, or changing routing identity.

A schema-30 lock crosses generation 31 through compatibility parsing: migration writes a lock without retired ADR routing keys and does not rewrite ADR files. Historical audit opens one repository and walks one requested range into an invocation-owned operation. The Git seam visits each rich commit once; audit immediately feeds it to incremental commit and aggregate rules and projects compact replay evidence. Audit validates compact commit identity and parent edges, then schedules selected children before selected parents with lexicographic revision tie-breaking; parents outside the selected range remain direct boundaries. Each scheduled commit interleaves stale-merge and transition replay while buffering their findings separately, then one live cleanliness read follows replay. External findings remain grouped as ordinary, stale, live, and transition; stale and transition paths share alias-aware canonical revision entries and cached load errors. Root transitions start from the empty universe, merge transitions use the first parent, and stale replay uses the result plus every ordered parent. On a historical cache miss, audit enumerates committed project-relative path and mode metadata without reading blobs. An absent `.awf/config.yaml` yields empty state; otherwise its light load reads only config and the optional lock, migrates and validates the committed config, and derives docs layout plus exact authority paths. A one-shot heavy loader reads and parses topic metadata, topic current-state parts, and top-level decision records only at the first universe consumer, then releases its captured selection. Exact selected reads fail closed, and the Selection remains type-distinct from the complete `snapshot.Tree` values used by current and staged checks. Revision keys can alias a first-parent canonical entry only when committed controls and paths prove irrelevance; `.awf` changes, changes under the parent's committed decisions directory, separately derived merge first-parent paths, and ambiguous evidence reload, and an out-of-range first parent loads directly without an ancestry walk. Scheduled per-key accounting aggregates aliases, clears sources after stale replay's final consumer, and clears the full heavy universe after its final consumer. Context cancellation and deadline expiry at range collection, committed evidence, revision derivation, stale or transition replay, or live cleanliness abort the operation with matchable identity instead of producing an advisory finding or allowing later work. For committed generation-31-and-later merges, audit derives the format active at the result generation and replays the shared cleaned-message trailer parser plus incoming-parent qualification; the separate merge relevance evidence does not alter ordinary merge changes or range semantics.

Pi context events sample the current model window and active branch at request time, copy request messages, and append one hidden transient line; no context fact is persisted or turns into pressure action. Handoff custom transcript ownership remains distinct even though Pi's current provider adapter converts custom content to a user-role request. For an associated Pi effort, the model tool calls the generated client, which invokes the binary's owner-scoped memory protocol; the binary returns shared human presentation only for owner-free commands, while owner-scoped JSON is the required byte-exact protocol. The client strictly decodes it, and the index applies association lifecycle and file-queue boundaries before returning the associated tool result.


<!-- awf:edit dependencies: from .awf/docs/parts/architecture/dependencies.md -->
## Key dependencies

- **`gopkg.in/yaml.v3`**: strict (`KnownFields`) parsing of the config tree and ADR frontmatter;
  unknown keys fail fast.
- **`encoding/json`, `crypto/sha256`, process execution, and filesystem primitives** (standard library): parse,
  fingerprint, and validate tracked configuration and local effort state without a database or background daemon.
- **`text/template`** (standard library): the rendering engine; ADR-0001 owns its
  publication-safety contract.
- **`github.com/go-git/go-git/v5`** (with `go-billy/v5`): the pure-Go implementation behind the
  seam's in-process object reads. Native `git` is a runtime and test prerequisite for repository
  control-root resolution, refs and worktree topology, and working-tree truth. Both are backends
  of `internal/git` and nothing else: no other production package may import the library or
  construct a git subprocess, and `internal/testsupport/gitfixture` is the single exception on
  the test side, which the zero-internal-deps rule forces rather than permits. The seam walks audit
  ranges through one rich-commit visitor without audit policy. Historical audit enumerates committed
  path and mode metadata through this seam without reading blobs, then its light load reads only
  configuration and schema controls. A one-shot heavy loader reads the exact ADR and topic authority
  selection at first use, releases its captured selection immediately, and the audit-owned alias-aware
  store releases sources and parsed universes at their separately counted final consumers. Exact selected reads reject unsafe, duplicate, missing, outside-root,
  and unsupported paths. First-parent changed paths are separate merge relevance evidence and never
  populate ordinary commit changes; current and staged checks retain complete snapshots and their full
  marker, coverage, and domain-sidecar projection.
- **`golang.org/x/mod`**: semver comparison for the binary-version gate (ADR-0039).
- **`github.com/pmezard/go-difflib`**: direct line change model for effort-owned Pi-compatible bounded memory display diffs; awf retains row formatting, offsets, context, and bounds.
- **`github.com/bmatcuk/doublestar/v4`**: the matcher behind `internal/pathglob`'s anchored
  full-path glob dialect: invariant source globs, dependency manifests, and domain `paths`
  all match through it (ADR-0077).
- **`golangci-lint`**: pinned as a `go tool` dependency and run by the gate (`./x gate`); this
  repo only, not part of the rendered standard.
- **`deadcode`** (`golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode`): pinned as a `go tool` dependency; the gate
  runs it (no `-test`) and `cmd/deadcodecheck` fails on any production function unreachable from a
  `main` outside `internal/testsupport/` (ADR-0063). This repo only, not part of the rendered standard.
- **Pi ai/TUI, coding-agent, Remote Pi, and TypeBox**: peer APIs used only by generated Pi extensions at runtime; adopters supply them and they are not awf-binary dependencies. Subagent and handoff factories retain their own guards. The selected `effort-workflow` Pi companion invokes the binary from the repository root, keeps its association process-local, and exposes fixed relative effort paths without changing CWD. The optional Remote Pi display-suffix event surface is consumed through awf-owned structural types: complete capability snapshots, payload-free requests, and string-or-null publication remain independent from complete advisory metadata. Missing or failing suffix integration degrades to metadata-only behavior and never changes routing identity.
- **Docker, Node, TypeScript, and c8**: pinned repo-only test dependencies under
  `tools/pi-extension-test/`; no host npm installation is used.
- **`gremlins`** (`github.com/go-gremlins/gremlins`): pinned as a `go tool` dependency; `./x mutants`
  runs it under the deterministic `.gremlins.yaml` config and `cmd/mutants` reports survived mutants
  (ADR-0066). Advisory only; never part of the gate. This repo only, not part of the rendered standard.

`internal/manifest` owns schema-sensitive lock decoding, while `internal/migrate` owns generation-31 removal of retired ADR routing payload.

- The generated context-usage extension uses the same pinned Pi runtime floor as handoff and subagents, but owns its local formatter rather than sharing subagent presentation code.

- **Pinned Pi runtime floor**: the retained fork-v0.81.1-awf.3 coding-agent artifact (embedded 0.81.1) supplies `getActiveTools`, `setActiveTools`, tool prompt guidance, and `withFileMutationQueue`; the effort companion guards these APIs before registration and uses the shared real-path mutation queue.


This checkout includes optional `commitPolicy` configuration. It is structurally validated and consumed by the generated reference-transaction and pre-push payloads. Configuration alone neither activates hooks nor protects a remote: preview intended history with `awf check commit-policy <revision-or-range>...`, then let adopter-owned, worktree-aware wiring invoke the inert payloads. The remote's receiving and branch policy remains the final boundary.
